title: The Cloud Promise Is Broken: Why Migrations Never End, Dashboards Don’t Change Anything & How To Fix Azure Responsibility Gaps

entities.name: Microsoft Azure
entities.quote: getting workloads into Azures the goal

quotes.text: The value of monitoring isn't in the report itself, it's in the decisions and outcomes it enables.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the core argument against data collection as busy work.

quotes.text: The fix isn't complicated whenever you assign responsibility paired with three things. Authority to implement changes, budget to cover them, and a clear service level expectation on how quickly those changes should happen.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete recipe for closing accountability gaps.

quotes.text: The practical lesson here is simple treat optimization budgets as permanent, not optional. Just as you wouldn't classify electricity or software licensing as temporary.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A clear budgeting recommendation for sustained cloud optimization.

quotes.text: A reactive stance assumes stability should be the norm and only prepares to respond when something breaks. A proactive stance assumes the cloud is always shifting, so it deliberately builds recurring time, budget, and accountability to act on that movement.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Crisply contrasts reactive and proactive cloud operations.

quotes.text: If you accept that migration never really ends, the question changes from are we done? To how quickly can we adapt?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes how success in cloud migrations should be measured.

takeaways: Cloud migrations do not end at go-live; treat ongoing change as the normal state of operations.
Tie every monitored metric to an owner who also has the authority, budget and access to act on it.
Fund cloud optimization as a permanent, quarterly-reviewed budget line instead of an optional second phase.
hook: Many organizations move to Azure expecting speed, savings and security, only to find that migrations never end and dashboards change nothing. This episode helps cloud and IT leaders close responsibility and budget gaps so that monitoring finally leads to action and continuous improvement.
